hypothesis: A causal conjunction of at least five consecutive completed one-minute decisions with structure support at or below -0.5 and an adverse completed-close return of 20-50 bps may reduce losses from persistently regime-opposed breakout-fade entries, provided it improves full-lifecycle after-friction outcomes rather than only truncating the currently losing v14 cluster.
decision: Reject promotion of the broad regime-opposition-plus-loss exit from this evidence and keep the active v14 runtime unchanged. Across 20 eligible all-live closed lifecycles, every tested threshold produced lower estimated net PnL than the actual exits; the least harmful 20 bps cell reduced net by $0.0994 and the 30-50 bps cells reduced net by $0.3612-$0.5994. The current v14 slice superficially favors earlier loss exits by $0.2081-$0.5764 across four resolved trades, but all four are losses from one short-only run and that post-hoc slice conflicts with the broader sample. Keep the policy report-only, retain venue protection on BTC, ETH, and SOL, preserve the inactive v21 routing candidate, and re-evaluate only after the three open lifecycles resolve. This revision does not place, close, resize, gate, restart, or promote anything.
falsifier: The technical result is falsified by any mismatch in lifecycle identity, completed-close/next-open alignment, fill and funding reconciliation, or immutable ledger hashes. The rejection should be updated if a predeclared prospective, non-overlapping, profile-matched and bidirectional sample shows positive after-friction candidate-minus-control expectancy with improved drawdown across multiple independent entry clusters rather than one symbol or one correlated burst.
limitations: The challenger was formulated after observing persistent opposition in the current v14 cluster, so the current-run improvement is post-hoc and cannot be treated as a holdout result.
The all-live sample mixes provider versions and profile eras; it is useful for falsifying a universal exit but not for estimating the exact v14 policy's prospective expectancy.
Only 20 closed lifecycles have causal price coverage, and several belong to correlated same-direction entry bursts rather than independent trials.
Closed counterfactuals reuse each actual exit's fill-to-reference ratio and fee rate; open counterfactuals use adverse entry slippage as an exit-slippage proxy.
One closed lifecycle lacks causal observations, and each current open lifecycle has one missing price pair explicitly excluded from its persistence sequence.
BTC, ETH, and SOL remain open, so their actual exit prices, fees, funding, MFE, MAE, and net outcomes can still change.
All four resolved v14 trades and all three current open trades are short, so this evidence does not establish bidirectional exit behavior.
The counterfactual summarizes overlapping lifecycles independently and does not claim a recomputed shared-portfolio equity curve.
No live strategy, position, order, stop, target, sizing policy, backend process, checkpoint process, or portfolio configuration changed as a result of this revision.
